title: Help from a Non-Muslim • The Rulings That Came at Khaybar • News First, Then the Foot • Ranks, Arrows and Timing • Supplies, Wealth and Tending the Wounded • The Commander-in-Chief • This Chapter in Hanafi Fiqh • Final Word

blocks.1: On the road to Badr, at Harrat al-Wabarah, a man came and joined; he was known for courage and bravery. The Companions were pleased to see him. The man said, I have come to go with you, I will get what is to be got with you. The Prophet {{1}} asked, do you believe in Allah and His Messenger? He said, no. He said,
blocks.3: Then go back; I will not seek the help of a polytheist.{{1}}
blocks.4: On the way he came two more times; both times the same question, the same answer. The third time, arriving at Bayda’, he said, yes, I believe. The Prophet {{1}} said, then come. On the road to Uhud too, a group of Jews, allies of Ibn Ubayy, were turned back with the same words; they did not accept Islam.{{2}}
blocks.5: Yet this same Prophet {{1}} had hired a polytheist of Banu al-Dil to show the way of the hijrah; he had put into his hands his own camel and Abu Bakr’s (RA). That is in dars eleven. And at Hudaybiyah it was Budayl of Khuza‘ah who brought the news of Quraysh, who had not yet become Muslim; Khuza‘ah were the Prophet’s {{2}} trusted well-wishers in Tihamah.{{3}}
blocks.6: Then how do the two statements fit together? The Hanafi jurists, joining the two incidents, have said: help of non-Muslims in fighting will not generally be taken, because the fear of betrayal remains; but if the Muslims are compelled, it may be taken. And in work outside the fighting, such as showing the way, building roads, digging trenches, there is no harm in using the skill of a trustworthy non-Muslim.{{1}}
blocks.7: The Prophet {{1}} turned that man of Badr back three times; in the end he joined the party with faith. The skill of a trustworthy person has value whatever his religion; a polytheist had shown the way of the hijrah. But it is not handing over the reins of one’s own decision to another.
blocks.8: The Rulings That Came at Khaybar
blocks.9: The day of Khaybar. A long siege, a hungry army. People found some donkeys outside the settlement and slaughtered them; meat was boiling in the pots. One came and said, the donkeys are being eaten. The Prophet {{1}} stayed silent. He came again and said it. Again silence. The third time he said, the donkeys are finished! Then the Prophet {{2}} sent a herald. The herald announced,
blocks.11: Allah and His Messenger forbid you the meat of domestic donkeys; for it is impure.{{1}}
blocks.12: At once the pots were overturned; the meat still boiling. A hungry army, the cooking almost done. Yet no one said, let us at least eat today’s. That very day permission for horse meat came; and the prohibition of mut‘ah marriage came.{{1}}
blocks.13: One Sa‘ of Dates for Two Sa‘
blocks.14: After the conquest of Khaybar one man was sent to be in charge there. One day he brought dates of a very fine kind for the Prophet {{1}}. The Prophet {{2}} asked, are all the dates of Khaybar like this? He said, by Allah, no, O Messenger of Allah. We take one sa‘ of these for two sa‘ of mixed dates, two sa‘ for three sa‘. The Prophet {{3}} said,
blocks.16: Do not do this. Sell the mixed dates for dirhams, then with those dirhams buy the fine dates.{{1}}
blocks.17: Taking more or less of the same thing in exchange for the same thing; this is called riba al-fadl, a kind of interest. The prohibition came, and with it the lawful way too. The agreement of half the crop, keeping Khaybar’s land in the Jews’ own hands, and the incident of the poisoned goat will come in dars twenty-one. In the share of spoils too a rule was settled at Khaybar; the mounted fighter received more than the fighter on foot, a separate share for the horse.{{1}}
blocks.18: When a prohibition comes we often say, from next time; this one is already done. The pots of Khaybar were overturned that day while still boiling. And transactions like taking one sa‘ for two sa‘ in the market go on even today; with changed names, changed looks.
blocks.22: Whenever the Messenger of Allah {{1}} intended an expedition, he would conceal the real destination by hinting at another direction.{{2}}
blocks.23: Not a lie; only the real destination was not spoken aloud. The exception was Tabuk. A distant road, fierce heat, a large enemy; so that time everyone was told openly, so that each could prepare. Where secrecy is security, secrecy; where speaking openly is preparation, openly.
blocks.24: And news of the enemy must be known beforehand. At Badr, Busaysah (RA) was sent ahead to look for Abu Sufyan’s caravan. At the Trench Zubayr (RA) went forward again and again to bring news of the enemy; and on that night of cold Hudhayfah (RA) entered the enemy camp. These events have come in earlier dars.{{1}}
blocks.25: The one who was Allah’s Messenger, to whom revelation descended, he too had news brought first, then placed his foot. We decide first, enquire later. A job offer, a talk of marriage, a big purchase; news first, then the foot.
blocks.27: On the day of Badr, the enemy still far. The Prophet {{1}} told the archers,
blocks.29: When they come close to you, then shoot; and save your arrows.{{1}}
blocks.30: Most arrows shot from afar fall on the ground; the quiver empties, the enemy remains unharmed. In one small instruction, the reckoning of supplies and the lesson of patience, together. In the timing of the attack too there was a rule. Nu‘man ibn Muqarrin (RA) said,
blocks.32: I have been present in battle with the Messenger of Allah {{1}}. If he did not fight at the start of the day, he would wait until the winds began to blow and the time of prayer came.{{2}}
blocks.33: The sun declines to the west, the wind blows, the time of prayer comes; and then Allah’s help descends. Three incidents of choosing a place have come in earlier dars. At Badr the camp by the wells, at Uhud fifty archers at the mountain pass, at the Trench the trench. In all three the same thing; if the place is right, half the fight is won in advance.{{1}}
blocks.34: We spend all our strength on the very first blow. The one who is the teacher taught: save your arrows, shoot with timing.
blocks.35: Supplies, Wealth and Tending the Wounded
blocks.36: The Qur’an has given the instruction to prepare like this,
blocks.38: (O Muslims!) Prepare against them whatever strength you can and cavalry stations, by which you will strike fear into the enemy of Allah and your (present) enemy, and others besides them whom you do not know (but) Allah knows them.{{1}}
blocks.39: Strength does not mean only the sword; whatever strength is of use in the age. And the cost of preparation is to be supplied by the whole society. The Prophet {{1}} said,
blocks.41: Whoever equips a fighter in the way of Allah has himself fought; and whoever looks after the family of a fighter in the way of Allah well has fought too.{{1}}
blocks.42: For the one who could not go to the field too, the door is open. Buying one person’s shield; keeping watch over another’s home.
blocks.43: Those Who Drew Water and Bound Wounds
blocks.46: We used to be with the Prophet {{1}}; we would give water to drink, treat the wounded, and bring back the slain to Madinah.{{2}}
blocks.49: I went on seven expeditions with the Messenger of Allah {{1}}. I would stay behind them in the tents, cook food, treat the wounded, tend the sick.{{2}}
blocks.50: At the Trench, for the wounded Sa‘d (RA) a tent was pitched in the mosque itself, so that he could be looked after from close by; that is in dars eighteen.{{1}}
blocks.51: In the work of the religion we know the names of those in the front rows. But the one who drew water, the one who cooked, the one who bound wounds, their words too remain written in the hadith. The work that is not seen is written in the same ledger.
blocks.53: Some people of the Aslam tribe were holding an archery contest. The Prophet {{1}} was passing by them. He said,
blocks.55: O descendants of Isma‘il, shoot; your father too was an archer. Shoot, I am with such-and-such group.{{1}}
blocks.56: The other group stopped their hands. The Prophet {{1}} asked, what happened, why are you not shooting? They said, if you are with their group, how can we shoot! He said, shoot, I am with all of you. In the contest he put his name down with one group; when the other group drew back its hands, he became both groups’. Let training go on, but let no one’s heart be broken. Standing on the minbar he recited that verse of al-Anfal, then said three times,
blocks.58: Know that strength is shooting. Know that strength is shooting. Know that strength is shooting.{{1}}
blocks.59: And he said, whoever learns archery and then gives it up is not of us. The trained horses used to run from al-Hafya’ to Thaniyyat al-Wada‘; the untrained from the Thaniyyah to the mosque of Banu Zurayq.{{1}}
blocks.61: One night a sound of fear rose in Madinah. Anas (RA) told of that night,
blocks.63: The Prophet {{1}} was the most handsome of people, the bravest of people. One night the people of Madinah were frightened and went out toward the sound. On the way the Prophet {{2}} met them; he was already returning with the news, on the bare back of Abu Talhah’s saddleless horse, with a sword hanging from his neck. He was saying, do not be afraid, do not be afraid.{{3}}
blocks.64: While the people were setting out toward the sound, he was already returning with the news. And when the fighting was hardest, al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (RA) said,
blocks.66: By Allah, when the fighting grew intense we used to shield ourselves with him. And the brave one among us was the one who could stand beside him.{{1}}
blocks.67: The Companions took shelter behind him; yet he was the Messenger of Allah, whose promise of help had come from the heavens. That promise did not give him leave from preparation. Archery contests, horse races, news of the enemy, the reckoning of saving arrows; he did all of it as a man would.{{1}}
blocks.68: When news of danger comes, it is easy to send others and sit; the one in charge went himself and saw. And tawakkul does not mean giving up preparation; it is trust after preparation.
blocks.70: In brief, the rulings the Hanafi jurists have settled from the incidents of this dars. Fighting those to whom the invitation to Islam has not reached is not permissible before inviting them. Even to those to whom it has reached, inviting first is mustahabb. Jizyah may be taken from the People of the Book, fire-worshippers and non-Arab polytheists; for Arab polytheists, it is either Islam or the sword.
blocks.71: Women, children, decrepit old men, the crippled and the blind may not be killed. But if any of these enters the fighting, takes part by incitement or counsel, or is a leader by whose word people move, even if a woman or child, the ruling is different.
blocks.72: Betrayal, misappropriating spoils and mutilating corpses are haram. If needed, burning the enemy’s fortresses and cutting trees is permissible; when victory is nearly certain it is makruh. Even if there are Muslim prisoners in the enemy fortress, or the enemy makes children a shield, arrows may be shot; but the targets will be only the enemy’s fighters.
blocks.73: The aman given by a free Muslim man or woman to anyone is effective. No attack while a covenant stands; if it is to be broken, it must first be announced openly. One-fifth of the spoils for the set heads, the other four parts for the fighters. In Imam Abu Hanifah’s view the horseman gets two shares, the foot soldier one; in the view of Imam Abu Yusuf and Imam Muhammad the horseman three shares.
blocks.74: The decision on prisoners of war is the ruler’s, looking at the welfare of the Muslims. No one will kill another’s prisoner; taking him to the imam is better. And if bound by any treaty about prisoners, keeping that treaty is necessary.
blocks.75: Help from non-Muslims in fighting should not be taken, but if compelled it may be taken. The meat of the domestic donkey is haram.{{1}}
blocks.77: Some pictures remain from this dars. The two doors kept open before war. A woman killed in the crowd, and one question; this one was not someone to fight! A Caliph walking on foot beside the commander, who did not forget even the beehive.
blocks.78: Before Usamah a question again and again; did you split open his heart? Thumamah released from the mosque pillar, whose hatred became love in three days. A cloak that kept burning as fire. A woman’s refuge, which the Prophet {{1}} accepted as his own refuge. And a horseman’s call; wafa’, not ghadr.
blocks.79: Pots overturned with boiling meat. A commander-in-chief who rode a bare-backed horse and was first to return with news. What a heart that must have been, in whose teaching a Caliph remembered even the enemy’s beehive on a war march! At the very place where there is power yet no accountability, these rules put to the test most of all. So take one deed home from today’s dars.
blocks.81: The Prophet {{1}} bound even the power of the battlefield within limits; no hand on one who is not fighting, no sword if the Kalimah is recited, keeping the word when a word is given. Today I will ask myself a question: in the place where I have power yet no accountability, what kind of person am I really? Today at home, in the shop, or with a subordinate I will stop at such a place, where because of power I could have crossed the limit; I will not give up this stopping from today.

quiz.q: Where did the man who was turned back on the road to Badr first meet them?
o: At Bayda’
At al-Abwa’
At Thaniyyat al-Wada‘ at the edge of Madinah
At Harrat al-Wabarah on the road to Badr
quiz.e: First at Harrat al-Wabarah; the third time at Bayda’ he accepted faith (Muslim 1817).

quiz.q: Turning a polytheist back at Badr, and a polytheist guide on the hijrah; how do the scholars reconcile them?
o: The later event abrogated the earlier
This was a special ruling only for the Prophet ﷺ
Not in war; in peacetime everything is permissible
When compelled in fighting, and there is no harm in other work
quiz.e: al-Kasani: in fighting not generally, but may be taken if compelled; in work outside fighting there is no harm in taking a trustworthy non-Muslim.

quiz.q: In taking on a skilled non-Muslim, what is the dars’s lesson?
o: Never to be taken under any circumstance
If skilled, handing over the whole burden of decisions to him as well
Take him if trustworthy, with the reins of decision in one’s own hand
Taking him only on condition of accepting Islam
quiz.e: A polytheist had shown the way of the hijrah; but authority was the Muslims’.

quiz.q: On hearing the prohibition of donkey meat at Khaybar, what did the Companions do?
o: Overturned the boiling pots
Finished the cooking and ate
Gave the meat away as charity once cooked
Gave it up from the next day
quiz.e: ‘The pots were overturned, the meat still boiling’ (Bukhari 5528).

quiz.q: Against saying ‘this time is done, from next time’ after learning of a prohibition, which picture stands opposite?
o: Thumamah bathing and reciting the Kalimah
Mu‘awiyah’s (RA) army turning back
Stopping the archery contest
Overturning the boiling pots at Khaybar
quiz.e: A hungry army, yet immediate action.

quiz.q: When exchanging an old item at a lower value for a new one, what does the hadith of Khaybar’s dates teach?
o: No more-or-less exchange of the same kind, separate sales
Giving less for a good thing is allowed
If both parties agree, more-or-less exchange of the same kind is allowed
If it is of good quality, taking more is allowed
quiz.e: ‘Sell the mixed dates for dirhams, then buy fine dates with the dirhams.’

quiz.q: In a job offer or a talk of marriage, which lesson of the dars applies?
o: Save the arrows
News first, then the foot
Wafa’, not ghadr
Strength is shooting
quiz.e: Even the one who received revelation had news brought first.

quiz.q: What was the instruction to the archers at Badr?
o: Keep shooting from afar, do not stop
Shoot when they come close, save the arrows
Never give up the mountain pass
Begin shooting only when the wind starts blowing
quiz.e: ‘When they come close, shoot; save your arrows’ (Bukhari 3984).

quiz.q: Against the tendency to spend all one’s strength at the very start of a big task, which instruction stands opposite?
o: No wishing to meet the enemy
War is strategy
Shoot when they come close, save the arrows
Fight steadfastly when you meet the enemy
quiz.e: The instruction at Badr: reckoning of supplies and patience.

quiz.q: On how many expeditions did Umm ‘Atiyyah (RA) go?
o: Three
Five
Seven
Nine
quiz.e: ‘I went on seven expeditions with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ’ (Muslim 1812).

quiz.q: For people who could not go to the field, which door does the dars mention?
o: Only making du‘a from afar
Taking part in the distribution of spoils without going to the field
Sending news of the enemy secretly
Equipping a fighter or looking after his family

quiz.q: When one is given an unseen, behind-the-scenes duty in the religion’s work, what do the incidents of Rubayyi‘ and Umm ‘Atiyyah recall?
o: Unseen work too is written in the same ledger
Front-row work is the real work
Women’s work is limited to inside the home only
The reward for rear work is less
quiz.e: The ones who drew water and bound wounds, their words too are written in the hadith.

quiz.q: On whose horse did the Prophet ﷺ go toward the sound on the night in Madinah?
o: Zubayr’s (RA)
Miqdad ibn al-Aswad’s (RA)
Sa‘d’s (RA)
Abu Talhah’s (RA)
quiz.e: On the bare back of a saddleless horse, a sword at his neck (Bukhari 2908).

quiz.q: As one responsible in an organisation, which model of the Prophet ﷺ can be placed in a crisis?
o: Arranging comfort for everyone first
Going himself to get news of danger
Sending others and waiting himself
Staying silent until news comes
quiz.e: While the people were setting out, he was returning with the news.
